title: an older or hand-written block is replaced where it stands, keeping its added= value and every byte outside it
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D8 (setup instructions, defect N-18): a delimited, reversible JITSO block in the instruction files agents read
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-18, setup instructions). The file has a block marked `block=0 added=1` (no tail text) between two sections. `setup instructions --yes` replaces the lines from BEGIN to END with the current block (`block=1`, the same `added=1`) and leaves `# A`, the blank lines and `# After` byte for byte. The oracle has no `setup` command: it answers `unknown command "setup"` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so every expectation that needs this output or file effect FAILS on it.
